name: Greyish Pink
lede: Greyish Pink is a muted, dusty rose named by modifier grammar as greyish plus [[pink]], recorded by the 2010 xkcd color survey and found far more often in old paintings than its coverage of the archive alone would suggest.

sections.title: Greyish, plus pink
sections.body:
Our data classes Greyish Pink as a descriptive-modifier name, the hedge [[cement]] pulling the parent color [[pink]] toward neutral [1]. Our sources carry no history for this exact value beyond the 2010 xkcd survey, which asked online visitors to type a name for colors shown on screen [1].

It sits close enough to [[grey-pink|Grey Pink]], another xkcd-survey name, that the two are only 2.6 color-distance units apart, almost the same shade [2]. Further out, [[dusty-pink|Dusty Pink]] is more vivid, and [[puce|Puce]] leans redder [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our 23,781-painting archive, 52 paintings carry a color close enough to this one over enough of their canvas to count, about 0.22 per cent, as photographed, rarer than 64 per cent of our named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, by lightness rank, in 40 per cent of the 15 paintings where that lens applies, so varnish cannot fake the reading [3].

The earliest match in our archive is dated 1301, with others reaching to 1918, but the archive's thin early centuries make that a floor on when the hue appears, not a first sighting, and 709 years before the name itself was recorded [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment matches [3].
